intro: Codex has three approval modes that control how much it does autonomously vs. how much it asks you to confirm.

items.title: Suggest — Safest
items.subtitle: codex --approval-mode suggest
items.body: Codex shows you what it wants to do — you decide whether to apply each change. Best for unfamiliar codebases, high-stakes changes (auth, payments, migrations), or when you want to learn from the approach.

items.title: Auto-edit — Recommended Default
items.subtitle: codex --approval-mode auto-edit
items.body: File edits apply automatically; shell commands still need your approval. Best for day-to-day coding in your own codebase — you trust the edits but want control over side effects like installs or test runs.

items.title: Full-auto — Fastest
items.subtitle: codex --approval-mode full-auto
items.body: Everything runs without prompting — reads, writes, and shell commands. Best for CI/CD pipelines, scripted automation, and trusted well-defined tasks. Always use in a git branch, never on main.

items.title: New or unfamiliar codebase?
items.body: Use suggest. You want to see every change before it lands.

items.title: Routine task in your own project?
items.body: Use auto-edit. Safe default for most day-to-day work.

items.title: CI pipeline or scripted automation?
items.body: Use full-auto — but always gate with tests afterwards: codex --approval-mode full-auto '...' && npm test

sections.title: Setting a Default
sections.code:
# In your shell profile (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc)
export CODEX_APPROVAL_MODE=auto-edit
